interpretation.didCanonicalisationEliminateKnownValidat: PARTIALLY, AND THE REMAINDER IS NAMED. 2 item(s) moved from validator-rejected under v1 to accepted under v2, of which 2 carry a v2 verdict that matches gold. 2 item(s) are still rejected under both (g0ec0d43dad311a77, g877a05e6f5bba835); their rejection categories and reasons are listed in f4aInterpretation.persistentRejections. Validator acceptance is verifiability, never semantic correctness.
interpretation.didPromptV2ImprovePageVersusUnit: MIXED, AND MEASURABLE. The two variants give different verdicts on 10 item(s): 4 are corrections (v1 wrong, v2 right), 4 are regressions (v1 right, v2 wrong), 0 leave correctness unchanged and 2 involve a validator-rejected answer. Net verdict correctness is +2 over 49 paired items. Every row is in f4aInterpretation.verdictMovements with its gold.
interpretation.didPromptV2ImproveUnknownVersusNoCalibra: YES ON THE AXIS ITSELF; THE DAMAGE COMES FROM ELSEWHERE. v1 emitted NO on 12 axis answer(s), of which 0 matched gold; v2 emitted NO on 0. Dropping NO cost nothing, because no gold axis in this corpus is NO at all — the classes present are UNKNOWN/YES. Of the 7 axis regressions, 7 are a CONSEQUENCE of v2 moving the verdict to NOT_A_UNIT, which nulls all three axes by the output schema's own biconditional, and 0 are independent of the verdict. 6 axis answers are corrected. The UNKNOWN/NO calibration change is a gain; the verdict change is what loses axis accuracy.
interpretation.didPromptV2IntroduceRegressionsElsewhere: YES, AND THEY ARE NAMED. No validity regression: 0 item(s) moved from accepted to rejected. Semantically, page_kind 3, provides_language_learning_or_support 1, serves_incoming_international_students 3, serves_outgoing_mobility_students 3, unit_name_expectation 4, unit_type 3, verdict 4 regressed at least one previously-correct item; every gold id is listed in f4aInterpretation.regressionsByField. A net gain on one field does not cancel a regression on another, and neither is reported as an aggregate improvement.

It was created AFTER inference, was never visible to the model, and leaves the F0B inference freeze byte-unchanged.

PAIRED, per item: v2 nets +7 correct answers across 7 scorable field(s). Improved: page_kind +5, provides_language_learning_or_support +4, unit_name_expectation +4, verdict +2. Regressed: serves_incoming_international_students -3, serves_outgoing_mobility_students -2, unit_type -3.
Frozen gates: v2 loses 1 gate(s) v1 met (minUnitTypeAccuracy) and gains 2 (minUnitPagePrecision, minHardNegativeRejection). These thresholds are F0B's; none was invented, relaxed or re-tuned here.
Validator acceptance is reported separately and is NOT presented as semantic correctness: an accepted answer is a verifiable answer, not a right one.

F0B's leave-one-out rule STILL FIRES and is still reported in full: removing ge789b0f0aedc398c does change a gate verdict. It no longer BLOCKS, because the status it names — BLOCKED_PENDING_OWNER_GOLD_ADJUDICATION — was pending an owner adjudication that has now happened. The owner confirmed the existing label (UNIT_PAGE / INTERNATIONAL_MOBILITY_OFFICE) on the frozen document and rubric alone, with no model prediction and no metric effect in view, so every number above is identical to the pre-adjudication derivation.

The leave-one-out view is NOT evidence against the owner-confirmed primary label. It measures how thin a 14-item unit-type denominator is: one item is 7.1% of it, so a single removal crossing a 0.85 threshold is a statement about the denominator, not about the label. The primary metric remains the reported one.

KEEP_PROMPT_V1_AND_REVISE_V2 is the closest available enum member and it does NOT mean v1 passes. V1 fails frozen gates of its own; it remains the COMPARATOR while a new prompt iteration is designed. Nothing here promotes v1, authorises a HOLDOUT run, or declares any variant acceptable.
recommendationScope: This recommendation concerns the DEVELOPMENT split only. It authorises no merge to main, no HOLDOUT run, no production configuration change and no deployment.
